novelty_flags.label: thm:complete-saddle-duality and prop:centrosymmetric-reduction
novelty_flags.one_line: The claimed strict extension is only from the proposal-defined compact polyhedral centered subclass, not from the published Assumption-5 class, whose directional derivatives need not be polyhedral; state the result as an orthogonal asymmetric polyhedral regime or prove the required class inclusion.

soundness_flags.label: thm:tie-uniform-lan-transfer
soundness_flags.one_line: “widehat Z_n converges uniformly” has no stated convergence mode or joint coupling with widehat G_n, so it does not define the transfer needed for expectations of the data-dependent certified rule; require uniform total-variation/Le-Cam-kernel risk transfer or an explicit stable joint convergence condition.

Theorem 1 gives a minimax-regret rule and value under its regularity conditions, with the rule based on a hardest one-dimensional subproblem and applicable convex centrosymmetric setting.

source_verification_receipts.version: 2009 working-paper version of the 2012 Journal of Econometrics article
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies asymmetric Type-I/Type-II regret and derives exact finite-sample solutions for normal, Bernoulli, and bounded-outcome experiments.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace the asserted extension language with a theorem that either proves inclusion of the published centered class or explicitly frames the asymmetric polyhedral class as an orthogonal regime, then give the exact overlap map to Theorem 4.

Specify a uniform bounded-loss transfer condition for the joint pair (widehat Z_n, widehat G_n), such as a Le Cam kernel bound or uniform total-variation risk approximation, and derive the final regret display from it.

Promote the coexistence witness from a strictness example to a robust coefficient-neighborhood result with an interval certificate, so the non-index phenomenon is not only a single hand-designed game.

recommended_next_step: Revise the comparator claim and make the feasible LAN-transfer premise mathematically explicit; retain the asymmetric polyhedral saddle and coexistence questions as the field-tier kernel.
